title: The Moon-Cheese Cellar
story: Deep in a hillside cellar, the village of Thistlecombe keeps 240 wheels of moon-cheese to last the long winter. Curdlewight the Rind Gnawer has burrowed in, and he nibbles by a strict schedule: a big helping the first night, then a smaller bite of whatever is left. Mr 6 lights a candle, counts the shelves, and decides to out-plan the glutton instead of chasing him.
question: Curdlewight eats 3/8 of the 240 wheels on the first night, then eats 20% of the wheels that remain on the second night. How many wheels of moon-cheese are left after the second night?
solution: First night: 3/8 of 240 = 90 wheels eaten, so 240 - 90 = 150 wheels remain.
Second night: 20% of 150 = 30 wheels eaten, so 150 - 30 = 120 wheels remain.
That leaves 120 wheels of moon-cheese safe on the shelves.
praise: Finding 3/8 of 240 was exactly the right opening move — the only missing step was taking the 20% off the 150 wheels that were LEFT, not the original 240.
hint: Work one night at a time: how many wheels are left after the first night? That leftover pile is the one the 20% comes from.
victory: Mr 6 shows Curdlewight the arithmetic on a slate: at that rate he'd be out of cheese before spring. The gnawer bursts into tears, apologizes, and takes a job as the cellar's night guard — paid in rinds.
imagePrompt: A candlelit hillside cellar stacked with pale glowing wheels of moon-cheese, a round furry gnawing beast with crumbs on its whiskers facing a small brave numeral '6' knight holding a chalk slate, warm cozy lamplight.
